records.text: Paper card. Question: Can a 3D structured graphene metamaterial (SGM) be used as a selective solar-thermal absorber with high efficiency and omnidirectional absorption?. System: Graphene metamaterial on metal substrates (e.g. copper, aluminum). Processing: Laser nanofabrication, self-assembly graphene oxide (GO) coating, and photo-induced reduction technologies. Test conditions: Solar simulator illumination, temperature range from 20 °C to 1273 K, concentration factor from 1 to 1000. Findings: High solar-to-thermal conversion efficiency of 90.1%; Omnidirectional absorption capability; Excellent photothermal performance; High thermal stability; Water evaporation rate of 1.5 kg m−2 h−1; Solar-to-vapor efficiency of 96.2%. Mechanism: The SGM absorber exhibits both surface plasmon resonance and cavity effects to trap the incident light around the graphene metamaterial layer in the near field, leading to high absorption and conversion of light to thermal energy. Limitations: The structural parameters of the SGM absorber need to be optimized for specific applications, and the fabrication process can be improved for better control of the structure and properties. Future work: Further optimization of the structural parameters, exploration of different metal substrates, and scaling up of the fabrication process for practical applications. Quote: "the SGM strategy simultaneously tackles the major challenges of efficient solar-thermal absorber"
